answer: Here is what I would bring to your check-up, most important first. Several things are overdue, or the records do not agree with each other. 1) Hydrochlorothiazide: the hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026, after your sodium fell to 123. But the pharmacy record still shows it as active with refills left, your May 2026 eye clinic record lists you as still taking it, and the June 2026 visit note says to continue current medications without mentioning the stop. Your sodium on June 15, 2026 was 134, still a little low. Please ask your doctor whether you are taking this medicine and whether it should stop. 2) Repeat thyroid test: your TSH was high in March (7.9). The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks, and no repeat is recorded. 3) Lung nodule: a CT in October 2025 showed an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe. The radiologist recommended a non-contrast chest CT in 6 to 12 months, which means by about October 2026. No follow-up chest CT is recorded. 4) Kidney stone: the 4 mm stone from October 2025 is not recorded as having passed. There is no urology visit and no repeat urine test on file, and the urine test that day showed large blood. 5) Diabetes yearly checks: your last cholesterol panel was September 2025 (LDL 142, high). No cholesterol-lowering medicine is on your list, and no urine albumin test is recorded. 6) Vaccines: only one Shingrix dose (November 2025) is recorded, and the second dose is due 2 to 6 months after the first. No flu shot for this season is recorded. 7) Medication list: several entries duplicate each other (amlodipine, losartan, metformin, Claritin), and an old lisinopril entry still shows as active even though it was stopped for cough in 2025. Ask for a full medication review. Up to date: your diabetic eye exam (May 2026, no retinopathy), A1c 6.6% in June 2026, blood pressure at goal in June 2026, and a normal colonoscopy in 2019 with the next due in 2029. Some of these may have been handled outside the records I can see, so confirm with your doctor.
short: Please check whether you are still taking hydrochlorothiazide, which the hospital stopped in March 2026 for low sodium. Also overdue: a repeat TSH and free T4, a follow-up chest CT for a 7 mm lung nodule (due by about October 2026), the second Shingrix dose, and yearly cholesterol and urine albumin tests for diabetes.

items.says: Hydrochlorothiazide was stopped by the hospital in March 2026, but the records conflict on whether you still take it, and your June sodium is still low.
items.why: The hospital discharge said stop, while the pharmacy, the May eye clinic record and the June visit note do not reflect that. Low sodium on June 15 is a risk sign if the drug was restarted or never stopped.

knowledge.says: For a single solid nodule of 6 to 8 mm, the Fleischner approach is a CT at 6 to 12 months, and often a further CT at 18 to 24 months. Her never-smoker history makes the risk lower, but the follow-up is still the standard step.
knowledge.guideline: Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines for incidental pulmonary nodules.
